World Forge · assessment · 17 September 2026

AETHER-0004

A good regional world. Keep the continent and tectonic system; focus the next generation pass on consistent lake state and smoother climate transfer.

Exact saved configuration · 655,362 surface cells · 40,962 process cells
Published source 47a6312ce473a60ec22a5bed301ab670ed2bf7da · application 2.11.1 · generator 2.10.0

66.34%Ocean area
7,856 mHighest terrain cell
998Selected river systems
240Mineral deposits

The continent shapes, regional relief, climatic contrasts and connected water networks are useful foundations for worldbuilding. My judgment is that another broad terrain rewrite would have low value here. The clearest remaining weaknesses lie where independently simplified models meet: partial lake coverage becomes a binary land class, frozen precipitation becomes lake input, and coarse rainfall is copied into fine cells.

Keep

What is already working

Two dominant landmasses contain about 66.0 and 56.9 million km², including their inland lakes, alongside substantial smaller continents and islands. Dry-land mean elevation is 827 m; 8.4% of dry land exceeds 2,000 m and only 0.14% exceeds 5,000 m. This snapshot does not justify another general reduction in mountain height.

The river graph has 971 systems ending at the ocean and 27 at closed lakes, with no unexplained terminal system. The global annual drainage ledger closes to approximately 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁴ relative error. This establishes numerical consistency, not physical calibration. Wetland fractions include marshes, swamps, fens and bogs, totaling about 5.25 million km². Their separate representation is useful.

Keep the compact resource model and local fertility potential. Mineral scarcity is asymmetric: 185 iron deposits, 29 copper, 9 tin, 11 gold and 6 corundum deposits. That is useful for later trade and settlement choices. The fertility index has a dry-land median of 23.4 and a 90th percentile of 46.3; those are relative prototype scores, not crop yields.

First pass · highest visible payoff

Use one fractional lake state across generation

Physical lake coverage sums to 11.11 million km², or 6.47% of non-ocean area. The current whole-cell lake class covers 9.05%—about 40% more area. Both metrics are area-weighted. The difference arises because a positive lake depth at a cell center can classify the entire cell as standing water, even when its modeled wet fraction is small.

This affects generation as well as appearance: the same binary rule gives zero fertility to lake-classified cells. Within those cells, the lake-coverage field still describes 5.59 million km² of uncovered land. Conversely, some cells classified as land contain fractional water. Shoreline cells need a shared mixture of land and water across ecology, fertility and the surface material.

Recommended change: make physical wet coverage the shared input to land suitability and shoreline appearance. Preserve exposed land within mixed cells. Retain the existing connected river and reservoir graph.

AETHER-0004 also contains very broad shallow lakes. Basin #2260 holds 247,276 km² of water at 1.57 m mean depth; #1701 holds 167,426 km² at 1.90 m. This makes them good candidates for a persistent-water core, seasonally wet margins and wetland habitat. Their actual seasonal behavior needs to be calculated; shallow depth alone does not establish that a lake dries or becomes marsh. EPA’s wetland descriptions support distinguishing shallow, variably inundated margins from deeper open water.

The largest lake is 1.83 million km² and about 195 m deep on average. Its size can be a distinctive inland sea for this world. Lake abundance alone is not a reason to erase it or force an Earth percentage.

Relevant code: generation/ecology.ts, generation/fertility.ts, generation/lake-surfaces.ts, render/SurfaceHabitats.ts. Existing basin shaping and sediment infill can produce broad flat floors; preserve their water accounting while unifying how the resulting footprint is interpreted.

First pass · water consistency

Share snow and seasonal storage with lakes

The land budget stores snowfall and releases meltwater. Lake balancing instead receives the full annual precipitation field as liquid input. Approximately 225,000 km² of modeled lake coverage lies in cells whose warmest sampled season stays below 0°C. The renderer already tints cold lakes toward ice; the unresolved issue is the water calculation.

For northern lake #464, direct precipitation supplies 9,175 m³/s while catchment inflow supplies 949 m³/s; modeled outflow is 9,098 m³/s. Roughly 36% of its mapped wet footprint remains below freezing in all four samples. These measurements do not establish the correct discharge, but the code confirms that snowfall storage is bypassed for direct lake precipitation. USGS describes the storage and delayed release of snowfall.

Recommended change: reuse the existing seasonal rain/snow/melt accounting for reservoir inputs, then add a small four-season storage calculation per lake. Derive wet extent and spill timing from that shared state. This would also support the shallow-lake margins above. Snow remaining frozen should stay in storage; lake liquid beneath ice can still receive and discharge water.

Relevant code: generation/land-water.ts, generation/drainage.ts, generation/reservoir.ts, generation/rivers.ts. Current seasonal river flows are normalized to the annual drainage solution, so correcting the annual liquid input must precede trusting revised seasonal release.

Second pass · regional transitions

Interpolate rainfall conservatively onto the surface

Every fine cell assigned to the same process cell receives identical seasonal rainfall. Across non-ocean neighbor pairs, the mean annual rainfall difference is 0 mm within one process cell and 190 mm across process-cell boundaries; the latter’s 95th percentile is 795 mm. Some strong real rain shadows are expected, but the repeated polygon boundaries come directly from the transfer scheme.

Recommended change: use a nonnegative interpolation that preserves each coarse region’s rainfall volume. Keep terrain-dependent temperature and meaningful rain shadows. This should make moisture, vegetation and fertility transitions less blocky without increasing climate resolution. It needs a focused before/after comparison; the expected visual improvement is a recommendation, not a measured result.

Desert covers 3.52% and savanna 17.71% of non-ocean area. The result is relatively green, but geography and this preset can legitimately produce that. I would first improve field transfer and water consistency, then decide whether the dry-climate preset needs adjustment.

Relevant code: generation/land-water.ts, particularly the conservative but piecewise-constant rainfall prolongation. The median surface-neighbor spacing is still about 30 km; this is regional environmental detail.

Before settlement scoring

Distinguish lake water from dependable freshwater

There are 299 closed lakes, together covering about 1.06 million km². Fertility currently assigns an accessible inland shore a freshwater contribution regardless of the lake’s water balance. Lake #3426 alone is a closed basin covering about 203,073 km².

Recommended change: add a simple freshwater-suitability or salinity-potential flag using throughflow and evaporative concentration, and use it for the shoreline bonus. Keep river mouths and incoming freshwater corridors distinct. A closed lake is not automatically saline; its history and chemistry are unresolved. USGS notes the association between lakes without river outlets and saline water.

Relevant code: generation/fertility.ts and the existing Lake inflow/outflow/evaporation fields. A compact classification is sufficient for this prototype; detailed chemistry is not a prerequisite.

Optional · map character

Coordinate river bends across several reaches

In this exact config, 30.8% of reaches above 1,000 m³/s have a course-length/endpoint-distance ratio below 1.01. That initially looks concerning, but most are associated with unsuitable terrain or water margins. Restricting to 1,882 large gentle reaches away from lakes and ocean leaves only 0.11% essentially straight, with median sinuosity 1.095.

The remaining limitation is shape construction: each grid edge receives its own bounded sinusoidal bend and seeded variation. The recent renderer smooths connected courses, but generation still lacks coherent migration over several edges. If stronger meanders remain a visual priority, generate one continuous curve per connected reach between important junctions, vary its wavelength and amplitude with valley space, and share it with bank shading and cutoff placement. Preserve real confluences and outlets. NPS describes meandering as lateral erosion and deposition along a valley.

Relevant code: generation/river-courses.ts. Sinuosity here is measured per generated grid edge before display smoothing; it is not a whole-river sinuosity measurement. The saved settings use bank mobility 1 and fluvial duration 1 Myr, not maximum settings.

Simplifications worth keeping

Spend complexity where it changes the result

Keep prescribed plate motion, seeded volcanism, compact mineral presets and subcell wetland fractions. Consolidating the lake state removes conflicting assumptions and has more immediate value than expanding those geological models. Keep the existing physical rainfall and water-volume accounting while refining their spatial and seasonal interpretation.

The full run took 219.5 seconds in this runtime. The two climate solves took 169.5 seconds, or 77%. River incision, course/delta construction, ecology and minerals/fertility together took about 2.8 seconds. Retained typed-array buffers total about 534 MB, excluding renderer allocations and peak generation memory.

Use the existing lower-resolution settings for exploration. If generation speed becomes the next priority, investigate reusing climate setup or reducing provisional-climate work, with a before/after geographic comparison. Removing inexpensive river or mineral features would barely affect this run’s time. These timings are environment-specific; no browser timing or visual QA was performed.

Suggested stopping point: finish shared lake coverage and snow/seasonal water accounting, then conservative rainfall transfer and freshwater suitability. Reassess AETHER-0004 plus a contrasting dry world. The continent system is already good enough to retain.

Evidence and reproducibility

Scope of this evaluation

One exact full-resolution regeneration from the original AETHER-0004 JSON, loaded through the current project importer. The original file identifies generator 2.9.0; the importer fills the current deposit-frequency and amount defaults at 1. This review uses the source snapshot matching the current published Site. It is an evaluation, with no implementation or publication changes.

Areas use spherical cell weights. “Non-ocean” includes inland lakes; “dry land” excludes the current lake biome. Lake physical area is cell area × wet fraction, and mean lake depth is stored volume / water area. Counts, numerical checks and maps were derived from the generated snapshot. The maps use nearest-cell equirectangular sampling and do not reproduce the artistic rendering styles.

Cold-lake footprint percentages use cells incident to that lake’s wet corners and their wet-area weights; shore cells may include nearby water, so those per-lake fractions are approximate. The global frozen-lake fraction is directly area-weighted. River endpoint checks use lake-aware system IDs, including connections through spilling lakes.
